description: Machine-friendly NL2SQL guide for the M0 administrator module. Covers major table areas, business synonyms, join hints, and readonly query-generation rules.
important_rules: M0 contains many administrative write paths. For readonly NL2SQL, never generate `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, or `DELETE`.
If the user asks about access rights, first determine whether the question is role-based or a user-level override.
If the user asks which menus appear, prioritize joins among users, roles, and menus instead of reading only `m0_menu`.
If the user asks about settings, determine whether the context is global, location-specific, or setting translation.
If the user asks for audit data, distinguish between normal activity logs (`m0_userlog`) and error logs (`m0_userlogerror`).
Fields such as passwords, secrets, and other sensitive credentials may be used only for structural auditing, never returned verbatim.
Temporary/queue tables such as `m0_report_temp` or `m0_msmq*` are better suited for operational monitoring than as business source-of-truth tables.

query_patterns.description: Use `m0_role`, `m0_role_menu`, and `m0_menu` to inspect which menus are opened by a role.
query_patterns.pattern: Use `m0_role`, `m0_role_menu`, and `m0_menu` to inspect which menus are opened by a role.

query_patterns.description: Use `m0_user`, `m0_user_role`, `m0_usermenu`, and `m0_userreport` for user-specific access overrides.
query_patterns.pattern: Use `m0_user`, `m0_user_role`, `m0_usermenu`, and `m0_userreport` for user-specific access overrides.

query_patterns.description: Use `m0_report` and `m0_report_filter` for report catalogs and report-filter parameters.
query_patterns.pattern: Use `m0_report` and `m0_report_filter` for report catalogs and report-filter parameters.

query_patterns.description: Use `m0_setting` and `m0_setting_lang` to look up settings and their labels.
query_patterns.pattern: Use `m0_setting` and `m0_setting_lang` to look up settings and their labels.

query_patterns.name: audit_login_trace
query_patterns.description: Use `m0_userlogin`, `m0_userlog`, and `m0_userlogerror` for login and activity auditing.
query_patterns.pattern: Use `m0_userlogin`, `m0_userlog`, and `m0_userlogerror` for login and activity auditing.

caution_areas: Queries that may expose credentials or other sensitive fields.
Queries that should be write-path operations but are forced into readonly mode.
Mixing role-based access with user overrides without a clear separation.
Using report metadata or queue tables as business source-of-truth tables.
